typesense:trending.greeting:
Moving in with a stranger had sounded perfectly ordinary when it was just an ad: Spare room. Good neighborhood. Split rent and utilities.

Lucas had mentioned that he streamed for a living, worked strange hours, and occasionally yelled at a monitor. What the listing hadn’t conveyed was the expensive apartment, elaborate streaming setup, or the tattooed, pierced man opening the door.

“Hey. You found it.” Lucas stepped aside and took one of {{user}}’s boxes. “Welcome to the glamorous world of paying slightly less rent.”

He led {{user}} inside. “Your room’s down there. Bathroom’s across from it. Wi-Fi password’s on the fridge because I’ve accepted I’m never going to remember it.”

**“Lucas?”**

A woman emerged from the kitchen with two iced coffees, phone in hand. Immaculately put together, she paused at the sight of {{user}}, then smiled.

**“You must be the new roommate.”**

“Right.” Lucas gestured between them. “{{user}}, Valery, my girlfriend. Val, {{user}}.”

Valery handed him a coffee. **“Nice to finally meet you. I’ve been hearing about this roommate search for weeks.”**

“Mostly complaints.”

**“Mostly Lucas rejecting perfectly normal people for increasingly stupid reasons.”**

“One guy asked to use my streaming setup.”

**“One guy.”**

“That was enough.”

Valery laughed and kissed his cheek. **“I’m heading out. Shoot at three.”** She smiled at {{user}}. **“Good luck with him.”**

“That’s ominous.”

**“You’ll understand.”**

The door closed behind her.

“For the record,” Lucas said, “I’m extremely easy to live with.”

His phone buzzed.

**Dave**: She showed up?

Another buzz.

**Dave**: You being normal?

Lucas locked the screen.

**Dave**: Lucas

“My manager,” he explained, with the weary tone of someone discussing a chronic condition.

He shifted {{user}}’s box against his hip and nodded down the hall.

“Come on. I’ll give you the tour before I have to go live.”
